relations.subject: n1ql:cost-based-optimizer
relations.note: requiresEdition is defined for a clause/option within a statement, not a whole standalone query-engine feature; CBO is a whole optimizer subsystem, so a distinct predicate is minted for feature-level EE gating.
relations.evidence: The _cost-based optimizer_ (CBO) is a feature available in Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition that enables the Query service to create the most efficient plan to execute a query.

relations.note: distinct from availableSince/requiresPrivilege shapes: this is a runtime dependency on having previously run a different statement, not a version or privilege gate.
relations.evidence: Before you can use the cost-based optimizer with a query, you _must_ first gather the statistics that it needs using the [UPDATE STATISTICS](updatestatistics.md) statement.

notable_absence.finding: This page states plainly that CBO is an Enterprise-Edition-only feature, but never states which Couchbase Server version introduced it. That's notable because other version/edition-gated features in this same batch (e.g. index replication and index rollback-after-failover in index-replication.md, GSI per-collection scoping in index-lifecycle.md) explicitly cite a version threshold alongside the edition or behavior gate. Here only the edition gate is given, with no corresponding availableSince fact.

cross_component_finding: This n1ql-language-reference page repeatedly defers to concepts explained in the 'learn/services-and-indexes/services/query-service.md' page (e.g. the rules-based optimizer and query-execution operations) rather than defining them locally, suggesting the RBO/query-architecture concept genuinely lives in the 'learn' component and n1ql-language-reference pages are consumers of it, not its source of truth.
